title: The US now regulates renting AI chips, not just buying
description: A new US interim rule targets remote access to advanced AI chips in overseas data centers. Here's the cloud loophole it aims to close.

scenes.big: Renting AI chips is now regulated
scenes.say: The US is now regulating who can rent advanced AI chips, not just who can buy them.
Regulators describe a loophole. A data center abroad holds legally exported chips. A company rents that computing power over the internet and trains its models remotely. The chips never ship to them.

On November sixteenth, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security announced an interim final rule. Exporters now need a license to ship advanced chips to data centers worldwide that supply large amounts of computing power to companies in China and other restricted places.
It's an interim rule, meaning it takes effect first and opens public comment afterward. Data centers already serving restricted firms get a window to apply for licenses.
The key numbers, as reported. Sixty days for public comment, ninety days for affected facilities to get licenses. Follow for more of how this stuff really works.
